Lefties, look for the fastball early—Glasnow uses fastballs 53.9% of the time against lefties. Stay disciplined against breaking balls, especially with two strikes; his curveball has a 61.9% whiff rate. Tanner Scott and Alex Vesia are the left-handed bullpen arms to watch late.
reminders: Right-handed matchup results are based on a small sample.
Be ready for Tanner Scott or Alex Vesia late.

briefings.headline: Elder sets the tone with change of speed and location
briefings.message: Bryce Elder starts, with a 95-pitch limit and a six-inning target. Mix breaking pitches and changeups to Freddie Freeman and Max Muncy; avoid predictable fastballs, and keep pitches down to Edman. If Elder exits early, go to long relief first. Use Dylan Lee and Didier Fuentes in setup spots, and save Raisel Iglesias for the ninth when possible. Hold Brent Suter if you can after his recent workload.
reminders: Use breaking balls to finish Teoscar Hernández; don’t feed him fastballs.
If the starter exits early, start with long relief; avoid leaning on Suter unless needed.
